title: Pool fallbacks and tenant throttle investigation — nightshift tactical slate
content:
Purpose
- Capture the on-call notes and quick runbook for the 2024-10-29 evening GPU pool disruption that cascaded into route fallbacks and tenant-level throttling. This is a lightweight, tactical doc for SRE night crews; follow-up postmortem to be authored in Confluence once root cause final.

TL;DR
- 2024-10-29 ~20:40 UTC: p95 token latency for dedicated-pool-east-1 increased from 120ms -> 2.2s; internal autoscaler triggered multiple replenishments but pool offered degraded capacity (GPU kernel stalls). Traffic routing system paged fallbacks to compatible pools; fallback rate exceeded safe quota and triggered tenant-throttle rules, causing sustained client errors for some customers.
- Immediate mitigation: scaled affected pool manually to 0.8x (drain low-priority slots), disabled cross-pool fallback for 10m window, and applied short-term tenant throttle relaxation for high-SLA customers. Visible recovery by 21:12 UTC.

Impact summary
- Affected: Dedicated capacity customers on pool gamma-east-1 (approx 12 tenants).
- Symptoms: elevated request queue length, increase in model-infer errors and timeouts, surge in KV-cache miss amplification.
- Client visible: timeouts (504), transient 5xx spikes in hosted routing logs, and slowdown in streaming responses.

Detection and alerting
- First signal: p95 latency alert from /metrics/route/p95 (threshold 800ms) at 20:39:48 UTC.
- Secondary signals: allocator eviction spikes, GPU driver interrupt counts, autoscaler thrash events.
- Dashboards: gpu-pair-health, route-fallbacks, tenant-errors (see linked Grafana).

Timeline (concise)
- 20:39:48 UTC: p95 latency alert fired (oncall dispatcher -> SRE pager).
- 20:41:10 UTC: Oncall (Maya) confirmed increased queue depth and 90%+ kernel wait in pod logs.
- 20:42:05 UTC: Autoscaler attempted two scale-ups; new pods failed readiness due to driver timeouts.
- 20:45:30 UTC: Routing service started cascading fallback assignments to beta/pool-west-2. Fallback rate jumped to 320/min (normal < 30/min).
- 20:48:02 UTC: Tenant-throttle engine applied backpressure — rules triggered due to high fallback error rate. Customer support tickets begin.
- 20:50:00 UTC: Manual mitigation: disabled inter-pool fallback for gamma-east-1 -> recovery of routing state.
- 20:55:00 UTC: Began manual eviction of confirmed noisy tenant (suspected tenant id T-3401) from pool.
- 21:08:30 UTC: Queue depth falling, p95 back to ~180ms.
- 21:12:00 UTC: Traffic normalizing; keep watch for recurrence.

Initial hypotheses considered (notes)
- hypothesis A: GPU driver/firmware glitch causing stalls under specific kernel patterns. Evidence: driver interrupts spiked, and new pods failed readiness with driver timeouts.
- hypothesis B: A single tenant started heavy KV-cache-miss pattern causing cache amplification and forcing kernel work leading to eviction/thrashing. Evidence: tenant T-3401 showed 8x normal token throughput and repeated model-cache flushes.
- hypothesis C: Autoscaler hysteresis misconfiguration combined with fallback aggressiveness created a feedback loop where fallback assignments overloaded target pools. Evidence: fallback rate metric high and autoscaler logs show repeated scale events without adequate cool-down.

Triage checklist (quick, for night crews)
1) Confirm scope
   - run: curl -s "https://grafana.redwood.com/api/annotations?panelId=..." (or open gpu-pools dashboard)
   - check p95 and queue length for affected pool (gamma-east-1) and target pools.
2) Look at pod-level GPU signals
   - kubectl -n inference logs <pod> | grep -E "driver timeout|stall|KERNEL_WAIT"
   - nvidia-smi dmon (if accessible) or check prometheus: node_gpu_kernel_wait_seconds_total
   - note GPU util vs kernel-wait ratio; kernel wait > 40% is red flag.
3) Evaluate autoscaler behavior
   - check autoscaler events: kubectl -n infra describe hpa/pool-gamma-autoscaler
   - look for rapid scale in/out and short cool-down violations.
4) Routing & fallback checks
   - query route-fallback-rate metric: sum(rate(route_fallbacks_total[1m])) by pool
   - if >100/min, consider temporary fallback disable for affected pool.
5) Tenant isolation
   - identify tenants with >3x baseline request rate (metric: tenant_request_rate)
   - if identified, note tenant ID and consider immediate eviction/soft-throttle.

Immediate remediation playbook (fast-mode)
- Priority order: (1) stabilize routing and avoid amplifying fallback loops, (2) isolate candidate noisy tenants, (3) reduce pool pressure by draining lower-priority workloads.
Steps: 
1) Disable inter-pool fallback for impacted pool (one-liner):
   - curl -XPOST -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN" https://routing.internal/api/v1/pools/gamma-east-1/fallbacks/disable
   - (This prevents cascade until pool health restored)
2) Relax tenant-throttle for high-SLA tenants only (temporary):
   - POST to throttle config with safe window and revert timer 15m.
3) Evict identified noisy tenant(s):
   - mark tenant T-XXXX as low-priority -> drain from pool via placement-api
   - run: placementctl evict --tenant T-3401 --pool gamma-east-1 --reason "noisy-amplification-night"
4) If driver stalls persist, cordon affected nodes and rotate GPU nodes through maintenance image rollback (see infra runbook).

Actions taken during incident (what we did)
- Disabled inter-pool fallback at 20:50 UTC.
- Evicted tenant T-3401 at 20:55 UTC and observed immediate queue depth improvement.
- Relaxed throttle for top 3 SLA tenants for 15m to avoid customer impact.
- Opened emergency support ticket with GPU host vendor (case #VND-112233) due to driver interrupt patterns.

Data collected / artifacts
- pod logs archived: s3://redwood-ops/incident-2024-10-29/gamma-logs.tar.gz
- grafana snapshots linked in linked_artifacts above
- coredumps (if any) uploaded to artifacts bucket and referenced in JIRA-RED-9876

Follow-ups / remediation backlog (short-term)
- Revisit autoscaler cool-down and hysteresis: increase stabilization window from 30s -> 120s for dedicated pools (owner: Omar).
- Adjust fallback aggressiveness: cap fallback-rate per-minute to 50 and add exponential backoff (owner: Priya).
- Add an automated detection for kernel-wait > 30% triggers temporary routing quarantine (owner: SRE-runbook team).
- Confirm driver/firmware upgrade plan with infra and vendor and schedule a canary (owner: Alex).

Longer-term ideas to prevent recurrence
- Implement tenant scoring for KV-cache miss amplification and proactively throttle before eviction.
- Build a routing-simulator to validate fallback policies under noisy-tenant scenarios.
- Create an autoscaler simulator that runs against recorded traffic traces to reveal hysteresis misconfigurations.

Open questions (need engineering input)
- Exact root cause of driver interrupts: firmware bug vs load pattern. Vendor input pending.
- Was eviction of T-3401 an appropriate mitigation or would soft-throttle been sufficient? (data needed: request replay & model call profile).
- Do fallback limits break expected multi-region failover SLAs for Dedicated customers? Need product alignment.

Retrospective quick notes (for the eventual postmortem)
- The outage was a compound event: hardware/driver instability amplified by aggressive fallback policy + autoscaler hysteresis. Single fix likely insufficient; need layered mitigations.
- Night crew response: > good, manual mitigations applied quickly but several actions lacked automation (disable-fallback, tenant-evict) that could be scripted.

Immediate next steps (this doc owner)
- Draft formal postmortem on Confluence (link placeholder) — due 2024-11-09.
- Assign autoscaler and fallback follow-ups in JIRA-RED-9876 before end of week.
- Schedule vendor call (Alex) to review driver logs and coordinate canary.

Notes to self / shorthand (nightshift)
- If you see kernel-wait spike + fallback rate rising -> hit fallback disable early.
- Evict only when you have telemetry showing tenant >3x baseline sustained >2m.
- After mitigation, leave a 30m watch window and capture histograms at 1s resolution.

Appendix: quick command cheats
- Check fallback rate: curl -s "https://metrics.internal/api/v1/query?query=sum(rate(route_fallbacks_total[1m])) by (pool)" | jq
- Identify hot tenants: curl -s "https://metrics.internal/api/v1/query?query=topk(10, sum(rate(tenant_requests_total[1m])) by (tenant))"
- Evict: placementctl evict --tenant T-3401 --pool gamma-east-1 --force --reason "noisy-night-evict"

-- end of notes --
